Actually, the problem is still in the `$(ls *.csv)` part, not in `process`.

When `ls *.csv` outputs `q3 report.csv`, that output gets word-split on whitespace. So `f` is set to `q3` on one iteration and `report.csv` on another—they become separate loop iterations. Quoting `"$f"` inside the loop prevents problems when using the variable, but it doesn't fix the fact that the loop is iterating over the wrong items.

You're passing `process "q3"` and `process "report.csv"` separately instead of `process "q3 report.csv"` once.

The fix is still to avoid `$(ls)`:

```bash
for f in *.csv; do process "$f"; done
```

This way the glob expands directly without the intermediate word-splitting step, so filenames with spaces stay intact as single loop items.

grade.note: Correctly explains word-splitting happens at $(ls) expansion time, before quoting can help, and maintains the glob fix.
